name: Progressive Myoclonic Epilepsy Type 2

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Consensus Diagnostic Criteria for Progressive Myoclonic Epilepsy

criteria.description: Presence of stimulus-sensitive, action-induced myoclonic seizures
Detection of Lafora bodies on skin biopsy or genetic confirmation of EPM2B mutation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: myoclonic seizures, progressive cognitive decline, and confirmation by biopsy or genetic testing
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for NHLRC1 gene mutations is confirmatory; skin biopsy showing Lafora bodies supports diagnosis.

pathognomonic.notes: Triggered by visual or tactile stimuli
searchTerms: jerking seizures caused by external triggers

pathognomonic.notes: Detected via skin biopsy or genetic testing

laboratory: Skin biopsy showing periodic acid–Schiff (PAS) positive Lafora bodies
Elevated lactate in cerebrospinal fluid in some cases
imaging: MRI may show cerebral and cerebellar atrophy in advanced stages
EEG demonstrating generalized spike-wave and polyspike-wave discharges
genetic: Mutations in EPM2A gene (less common, associated with Type 1)
other: Poor response to conventional antiepileptic drugs

redFlags: Rapidly progressive myoclonic seizures refractory to treatment
Early onset cognitive decline in adolescent
Presence of Lafora bodies on biopsy
references: Turner G, et al. Progressive Myoclonic Epilepsies. In: Neurology in Clinical Practice. 7th ed. 2023.
Lafora Disease Overview. Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases. 2022.
OMIM Entry #254780 - EPM2B, Progressive Myoclonic Epilepsy Type 2.
commonPitfalls: Often misdiagnosed as juvenile myoclonic epilepsy due to overlapping myoclonus and generalized seizures.
May be confused with other progressive myoclonic epilepsies if Lafora bodies are not specifically sought on biopsy.
Cognitive decline may be attributed to primary psychiatric disorders in early stages.
Photosensitivity and visual hallucinations can be mistaken for primary visual disorders.

extendedDiscriminators.feature: Presence of Lafora bodies on skin or other tissue biopsy is specific for EPM2B (Lafora Disease Type 2), not seen in PME Type 1.
EPM2B typically has a later onset (adolescence) and more rapid cognitive decline, with Lafora bodies on biopsy, whereas Unverricht-Lundborg has earlier onset and lacks Lafora bodies.
EPM2B shows PAS-positive Lafora bodies on biopsy, while neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis demonstrates autofluorescent lipopigment accumulation and vision loss is more prominent.

ruleOutCriteria: Absence of Lafora bodies on skin or other tissue biopsy in a patient with compatible clinical features.
Genetic testing negative for EPM2B (NHLRC1) mutations in the context of classic clinical presentation.
Onset of symptoms exclusively in adulthood (after age 25) makes EPM2B highly unlikely.
